strings.name: Richard Thaler
strings.summary: Thaler tests rational-choice assumptions with psychological evidence, studying mental accounting, the endowment effect, self-control and financial behavior. He taught at Rochester, Cornell and Chicago, exchanged ideas with Kahneman and others, and co-authored Nudge with Sunstein. His work influences savings plans and public policy while raising debate about choice architecture and autonomy. He received the 2017 economics Nobel and later became a Chicago professor emeritus.
